editorial:
Imagine being a typical fifteen-year-old who just wants to break free from your parents. That is exactly where you find Emma, a girl who feels trapped by her family rules and is looking for any way to get some independence. To spice things up, she starts messing around with some dark rituals just for fun, not really thinking they are real. The vibe starts off like a normal teen drama, but it quickly turns into a nightmare. You get to watch Emma go from a rebellious kid to someone who is terrified of her own body as strange fits and scary behavior take over her life.

What really works here is the tension as the parents try to figure out if their daughter is sick or actually possessed. The acting feels real, and the slow build-up makes the scary parts hit harder. While some parts move a bit slow, the payoff is worth it for horror fans. If you are into supernatural stories, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night, or if you want the best picture, look for a 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection for those crisp, creepy visuals.
endingExplained: At the end, you discover that Emma's curiosity opened a door for a real demon to enter her soul. The family brings in a priest to perform an exorcism to save her. After a violent and loud battle between the priest and the entity, the demon is finally forced out of Emma. She survives the ordeal, but the movie leaves you wondering if the damage is permanent and if she ever truly escaped the darkness.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves possession movies and supernatural mysteries.
